purpose: Define the school-neutral engine boundary after pure-helper extraction, without changing Waseda production behavior or replacing Rikkyo's existing FSRS/storage architecture.
principles: The common engine must not own a school's storage key, database name, cloud endpoint, app id, export format, branding, score-band names, UI copy, or migration rules.
Scheduler strategy is injected. Waseda's current forgetting-curve model and Rikkyo's FSRS-6 model are separate valid adapter implementations; neither scheduler is silently reinterpreted as the other.
Item identity is supplied by the school adapter and remains stable. The common engine must not rewrite Waseda vocabulary ids or Rikkyo rik-* stable ids.

Question and planning behavior may share orchestration, but school-specific modes, score bands, study-layer meanings, priority policy, challenge policy and retry spacing remain adapter policy until explicitly normalized.
Persistence and cloud synchronization are separate boundaries from learning-policy extraction.
UI explanation strings remain outside the common engine.

engineOwns: generic queue traversal orchestration once school state has been adapted

firstRuntimeBoundary.name: memory-scheduler-policy-adapter
implementationResult: Waseda memory-policy adapter returns the exact reviewed Waseda retention and interval values.
The existing Waseda memory runtime delegates to the Waseda-only adapter without changing persistence.
Branch-head and synthetic-merge two-pass existing-user parity and ownership gates passed.
Rikkyo runtime and production main remained unchanged.
